description.default: Read-only checks of this PC: busiest processes, disk space, network, a service's state, an app's version and whether it responds, recent crash records, or what is playing (media). Changes nothing.

target.description: App process name or service name, when the check needs one

description.default: Find where a piece of text is in one open window (OCR first; the local vision model only if OCR does not find it) and say where, as a point inside that window. Read-only: it does not click. Says whether the place was OBSERVED (OCR read it) or only INFERRED (the vision model guessed). Refuses password managers, wallets and bank windows. UNVERIFIED on real hardware: written and tested against a fake console only.

app.description: The app's process name, e.g. notepad

text.description: The text (a button label, a heading) to find in that window

description.default: The owner's Chrome profiles Neko can use, with the names to say for each and a masked account. Ask the owner which one when a name fits more than one.
How the current or a named mission is going: steps done and checked, what failed, the explanation.

profile.description: Chrome profile alias: 'default' (the owner's default account) or a name such as 'VenkatAMV'; see list_browser_profiles.

description.default: Find a song or video on YouTube in the owner's Chrome and play it; reports the exact video and whether it is really playing (checked, not assumed). Example: 'play a Kalyani song'.

profile.description: Chrome profile alias: 'default' (the owner's default account) or a name such as 'VenkatAMV'; see list_browser_profiles.

query.description: What to search for on YouTube

description.default: Read the text of one open window by OCR (Windows' built-in text recognition), for a window whose accessibility tree gives nothing: a game, a remote desktop, a picture of a form. Less reliable than the accessibility tree (OCR misreads digits and letters), so say so when you rely on it. Read-only; refuses password managers, wallets and bank windows. UNVERIFIED on real hardware: written and tested against a fake console only. The text goes to the model only when the owner allowed screen text (NEKO_SCREEN_TEXT_TO_MODEL=1) AND the privacy gateway has hidden names, places and private details in it; secrets are removed first. Otherwise it is withheld.

app.description: The app's process name, e.g. notepad

description.default: What the PC monitor noticed recently: program crashes, low disk space, a local service that stopped, a stuck PC task. Use for 'is anything wrong with my PC?' or 'what did you notice?'.

ONLY when the owner asks, after Stop reported a PC operation still_running: free the PC lock of an operation that will not end. It succeeds only if that operation was asked to stop and the kernel confirms every PC job it had ended (or its process is gone); otherwise it refuses and says why. It never lets a second task act while the first may still control the desktop.

Continue a mission that stopped for the owner, with the same mission id: after the owner approved the waiting action in the JARVIS console with the PIN, with the owner's answer to the mission's question, or after an interrupted step (answer 'done' if it already happened, 'redo' if it did not). Steps already done are never repeated. Use this for 'continue the mission', never start_mission again.

answer.description: The owner's answer to the mission's question, or done/redo

mission.description: The mission id; empty = the latest mission

Paying, sending, deleting, signing out and similar clicks wait for the owner's approval.
